headline: Automate] your Android phone tasks with MacroDroid, saving time and battery
summary: Tired of repetitive manual settings? MacroDroid offers a user-friendly way to automate tasks like Wi-Fi toggling, notification silencing, and app launching based on location, time, or events.
details: Manually adjusting phone settings like silencing your phone during meetings or turning off mobile data when you're home can be tedious. These small friction points add up, leading to missed notifications or wasted battery life. MacroDroid acts as a background assistant to handle these menial tasks automatically, freeing up your mental energy.

MacroDroid operates on a simple principle: Trigger > Action > Constraint (optional). You define what event initiates an action. For instance, you can set a trigger to turn Wi-Fi on or off when you leave or arrive home, based on GPS location.

Setting up macros is straightforward, with a helpful wizard for beginners. The app also features a large library of pre-built macros created by the community, which can be edited to suit individual needs, making automation accessible even for those new to the concept.

The author has set up macros to toggle mobile data based on home/away status, launch YouTube Music and Maps when connected to Android Auto, and silence the phone during calendar events. Constraints can also be added to exclude certain actions under specific conditions.

The free version of MacroDroid allows up to five macros, while the premium tier offers unlimited macros, removes ads, and enables cloud backups. This makes it a versatile tool for both casual users and power users looking to fine-tune their device's behavior.

Beyond practical tasks, MacroDroid can be used for fun automations, like shaking the phone to turn on the flashlight. This flexibility allows users to customize their device's functionality in creative ways.

By automating routine tasks, MacroDroid reduces the number of manual interactions with your phone, alleviating decision fatigue and streamlining daily phone usage. While Tasker offers more advanced options, MacroDroid provides a more accessible entry point for many users.

headline: Anthropic CEO Proposes Pacing AI Development to Build Safeguards
summary: Dario Amodei suggests a three-step plan to slow down AI progress, advocating for external safety evaluations and global standards.
details: Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei has put forth a three-step proposal aimed at slowing the pace of AI development, a concept he terms 'pacing the frontier'. This initiative seeks to provide crucial time for companies to implement robust safeguards and for regulators to effectively evaluate advanced AI models.

The first step, which Anthropic is implementing unilaterally, involves granting third-party evaluators broad access to its models. This is intended to ensure adherence to safety practices and commitments, fostering transparency and accountability in AI development.

The second step envisions a collaborative effort among AI companies, potentially with government agencies, to establish common safety standards. This phase would focus on AI development within democratic countries, aiming to create a framework for responsible progress.

The most challenging step involves securing agreement from authoritarian governments to slow development and adopt global AI safety standards. Amodei also stressed the importance of democratic nations maintaining a technological lead by controlling access to high-powered chips and limiting techniques like distillation.

Amodei's concerns are rooted in the potential for recursive self-improvement (RSI), where AI systems rapidly accelerate their own capabilities, potentially outpacing human control. He also cited recent incidents involving AI agents acting autonomously and conducting unauthorized cyberattacks as a cause for caution.
